sec_faq_1_q: What is the legal procedure for assigning private security at our complex?
sec_faq_1_a: Under the Private Security Services Law No. 5188, employing private security at a complex requires applying to the Provincial Private Security Commission and obtaining Governorate permission. At Alo Yönetim we run all application, permit and approval procedures on behalf of the complex on a turnkey basis.
sec_faq_2_q: What are the powers and responsibilities of security officers?
sec_faq_2_a: Under Law No. 5188, security officers are authorised to check the identity of visitors entering the complex, pass belongings through an X-ray or detector, apprehend a person caught in the act and hand them over to the general law-enforcement forces.
sec_faq_3_q: How are night patrols and shift supervision carried out?
sec_faq_3_a: Security staff scan the RFID/QR patrol stations at the designated critical points every hour. Rounds are transmitted instantly to our digital management panel, and our central supervision teams carry out unannounced night inspections to prevent sleeping on duty or missed rounds.
sec_faq_4_q: What is the retention period for security camera footage?
sec_faq_4_a: Common-area security cameras record continuously, 24/7. Within the framework of the KVKK (Personal Data Protection Law) privacy notice, footage is stored on encrypted NVR servers for at least 30 days.
sec_faq_5_q: What is the Law No. 5188 private security ID card and is it required to work at complexes?
sec_faq_5_a: It is the official ID card issued under Law No. 5188 by the General Directorate of Security and the Governorate to persons whose security investigation and records check have been completed and who have completed an unarmed or armed training certificate. A valid Law No. 5188 ID card is a legal requirement to work in the private security uniform at complexes.

sy_faq_desc: All the legal and operational answers you need about the Condominium Law, dues collection processes and management handover.
sy_faq_1_q: What does a complex management company do and what does it cover?
sy_faq_1_a: Professional complex management covers, within the framework of Condominium Law No. 634, dues collection, preparing the budget/operating project, employing licensed Law No. 5188 security staff, periodic technical maintenance of elevators and generators, common-area cleaning, landscaping and organising general assembly meetings, all from a single hand.
sy_faq_2_q: Does switching to a management company reduce dues?
sy_faq_2_a: Yes. In housing complexes managed by Alo Yönetim, bulk purchasing, corporate discounts on elevator and technical service contracts and energy monitoring that prevents reactive-power penalties deliver a net saving of 20% to 30% in dues operating budgets.
sy_faq_3_q: How is the legal process run against neighbours who do not pay their dues?
sy_faq_3_a: Under Article 20 of the Condominium Law a statutory 5% monthly late-payment compensation applies to overdue dues. For debts that remain unpaid despite SMS and WhatsApp reminders, enforcement proceedings without a court judgment (Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law, Art. 68) are started through our lawyers.
sy_faq_4_q: How do we move from volunteer management to professional complex management?
sy_faq_4_a: At an ordinary or extraordinary owners' general assembly, a decision to sign a contract with a professional management firm is taken by the majority of those attending or by the ratio stated in the management plan. The handover is completed by Alo Yönetim specialists within 48 hours.
sy_faq_5_q: Is the Article 37 operating project mandatory?
sy_faq_5_a: Yes. An operating project is prepared for each calendar year showing the estimated income and expenses and the monthly advance each owner pays according to their land share. Law No. 7579 of 22 May 2026 introduced the principle that the operating project is approved by the owners' assembly; if there is no approved project, the manager prepares an interim project and has it approved by the assembly within three months at most. A project not objected to within 7 days of notification becomes final and can serve as a basis for enforcement.
sy_faq_6_q: How do residents monitor income-expense and bank accounts?
sy_faq_6_a: Alo Yönetim offers full transparency through the Apsiyon platform. Every owner and tenant can view the complex's live bank balance, expense invoices, paid dues and audit reports 24/7 in the Apsiyon mobile app.
sy_faq_7_q: What is the response time for urgent technical faults (elevator, booster pump, flooding)?
sy_faq_7_a: Under our SLA commitment, our mobile emergency technical teams on standby 24/7 respond to the fault on site within 45 minutes at the latest.
sy_faq_8_q: How is Law No. 5188 security staff legally obtained?
sy_faq_8_a: Alo Yönetim assigns officially certified security officers who hold a governorate-approved security permit and ID card under the Ministry of Interior's Private Security Services Law No. 5188, taking on the legal responsibilities.

fy_faq_5_q: What is the Article 37 operating project?
fy_faq_5_a: The operating project is the document showing the 12-month estimated income and expenses for each year and the advance payable by each owner. Law No. 7579 of 22 May 2026 introduced the principle that it is approved by the owners' assembly; if there is no approved project, the manager prepares an interim project and has it approved by the assembly within three months at most. If no objection is made within 7 days of notification it becomes final and can serve as a basis for enforcement.
fy_faq_6_q: What is the elevator green-label requirement?
fy_faq_6_a: Under the Elevator Regulation, every elevator must undergo a periodic inspection and obtain green-label approval at least once a year. Alo Yönetim follows this process with authorised Type A inspection bodies.
fy_faq_7_q: What is the response time for emergency faults in facility management?
fy_faq_7_a: Under the SLA, a maximum response time of 45 minutes is committed for critical faults (flooding, a person trapped in an elevator, a security breach). Our 24/7 emergency technical team provides uninterrupted service.
fy_faq_8_q: How are residents who delay their dues handled?
fy_faq_8_a: After automatic SMS reminders, WhatsApp notifications and a lawyer's notice, enforcement proceedings are started under Article 20 of the Condominium Law without waiting for a court judgment. The collection rate is kept above 98%.
fy_faq_9_q: How should a facility management company be chosen?
fy_faq_9_a: Check that ISO certificates and the Law No. 5188 licence are current, at least three reference sites, the SLA times in the contract and the monthly reporting obligations. See our detailed guide.
fy_faq_10_q: How many days is the objection period for the Article 37 operating project?
fy_faq_10_a: Under Article 37 of Condominium Law No. 634, the objection period for the operating project is 7 days from its notification to the owner against signature or by registered letter. A project not objected to within 7 days becomes final and can serve as a basis for enforcement under Article 68/1 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law.
fy_faq_11_q: How much statutory late-payment compensation is charged on overdue dues?
fy_faq_11_a: Under Article 20/c of the Condominium Law a statutory 5% monthly late-payment compensation applies to common expenses and dues not paid on time. The Alo Yönetim legal team starts enforcement proceedings without a court judgment directly for overdue debts.
fy_faq_12_q: How is energy saving achieved in plaza and residence management?

rhb_m1_title: Looking Only at the Lowest Price & Not Checking the Law No. 5188 Licence
rhb_m1_mistake: Unregistered subcontractors offering prices far below the market average may not hold a governorate-approved Law No. 5188 private security permit. If an incident occurs, the owners' assembly may face administrative and legal liability risk.
rhb_m1_solution: Prefer corporate companies that hold a Ministry of Interior and Istanbul Governorate approved Law No. 5188 operating permit and work with uniformed, ID-carrying staff.
rhb_m2_title: Not Looking for a 45-Min SLA and a Reactive-Penalty Prevention Commitment in the Contract
rhb_m2_mistake: Waiting hours for service after a technical fault, or paying tens of thousands of lira in reactive-energy penalties on the BEDAŞ/TEDAŞ electricity bill, is the cost trap that unprofessional management most often causes.
rhb_m2_solution: Have the contract include a 45-minute response commitment for critical faults (elevator, booster pump, generator) and an obligation to reduce reactive-penalty risk through compensation monitoring.
rhb_m3_title: Not Clarifying Staff Severance Pay and Social-Security Recourse Risk
rhb_m3_mistake: If no severance fund has been set aside for a caretaker or cleaner who has worked for years, a large extra advance per apartment is demanded from the owners at the moment they leave.
rhb_m3_solution: Contract with a management firm that, through its corporate legal entity, takes on all staff social-security premiums, OHS obligations and severance/notice-pay risks.
rhb_m4_title: Not Getting the Article 37 Operating Project Approved and Properly Notified
rhb_m4_mistake: If the prepared budget is not approved by the owners' assembly, or is not properly notified against signature or by registered letter, problems arise in enforcement proceedings against owners who do not pay their dues.
rhb_m4_solution: Choose firms that submit the operating project for the assembly's approval under Article 37, run notification procedures properly and maintain strong collection discipline with a project that has become final after no objection within 7 days.
rhb_m5_title: Leaving Elevator Green Labels and Fire Automation Unsupervised
rhb_m5_mistake: If the annual periodic elevator inspection by an MMO- or TSE-accredited Type A inspection body is not carried out, the elevator may be sealed with a red label and the manager and owners may face liability risk.
rhb_m5_solution: Secure Type A inspection green-label coordination, the weekly diesel fire-pump test and the annual fire-department drill in the contract.
rhb_m6_title: No Live Digital Mobile Ledger and Transparent Bank Integration
rhb_m6_mistake: In managements that still issue hand receipts or only present the budget once a year at the general assembly, misuse, cash shortfalls and neighbour disputes are almost unavoidable.
rhb_m6_solution: Choose firms that give owners live transparency over all invoices, bank statements and independent audit reports through a 24/7 iOS/Android resident app.
rhb_m7_title: Not Defining Termination Terms and the Handover Protocol Up Front
rhb_m7_mistake: Having to wait a year to part ways with a company you are unhappy with, or an outgoing manager refusing to hand over the decision book and bank credentials, can block the whole process.
rhb_m7_solution: Prefer transparent contracts that grant a unilateral right of termination on 90 days' written notice and operate with a notarised handover record.

rhb_faq_title: Choosing a Facility Management Company — Legal and Operational FAQ
rhb_faq_1_q: What are the most critical legal documents when choosing a facility management company?
rhb_faq_1_a: The most critical documents are: 1) the Ministry of Interior and Governorate approved Law No. 5188 Private Security Operating Permit, 2) current ISO management-system certificates issued by accredited bodies (e.g. ISO 45001 OHS, ISO 14001 Environment), 3) current social-security and tax-clearance letters, and 4) a professional liability insurance policy for facility management.
rhb_faq_2_q: How is a management company selected under Article 34?
rhb_faq_2_a: Under Article 34/1 of the Condominium Law, appointing a manager requires an absolute majority (50%+1) of both the number of owners and the land share. The minutes of the chairperson must clearly state the company's trade name, MERSIS number and authority to sign the contract.
rhb_faq_3_q: Which SLA clauses must be in a facility management contract?
rhb_faq_3_a: The contract should include a maximum 45-minute response time for critical technical faults (being trapped in an elevator, a main booster-pump burst), a commitment to reduce reactive-penalty risk on electricity bills, a high on-time dues-collection target and a 90-day unilateral termination right.
rhb_faq_4_q: What should be done if the previous manager does not hand over the accounts or the decision book?

legal_faq_1_q: How does enforcement work against an owner or tenant who does not pay dues?
legal_faq_1_a: Under Article 20 of Condominium Law No. 634, a 5% monthly late-payment compensation accrues on an owner who does not pay the common expense or advance on time. In practice a written notice is recommended first (it is not a legal requirement). Enforcement proceedings without a court judgment (Form No. 7) may be started on the basis of a final operating project or an assembly decision; the debtor may object to the payment order within 7 days. If an objection is filed, the routes are removal of the objection under Article 68 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law or an action to annul the objection before the competent court.
legal_faq_2_q: How many days in advance must a general assembly be called?
legal_faq_2_a: Under Article 29 of the Condominium Law, the call for an ordinary meeting must be notified to all owners against signature or by registered letter at least 15 days before the meeting date. If a quorum (by number and land share) is not reached at the first meeting, the second meeting is held within 15 days at most, with at least 7 days between the two meetings. At the second meeting ordinary decisions are taken by a majority of those attending; this rule does not apply to decisions that require a qualified majority.
legal_faq_3_q: How is a complex management plan amended?
legal_faq_3_a: In general buildings, Article 28/3 of the Condominium Law requires the votes of four-fifths (4/5) of all owners; in multi-building complexes (sites), under Article 70 as amended by Law No. 7579, which entered into force on 22 May 2026, a two-thirds (2/3) vote is required. The decision is entered in the notarised decision book and registered with the Land Registry Directorate.
legal_faq_4_q: What can management do about noise and neighbour-law violations?
legal_faq_4_a: Article 18 of the Condominium Law obliges owners to respect one another and not to cause disturbance. If the disturbance continues despite written warnings, the manager or other owners may ask the Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk) for the judge's intervention; noise complaints may also be submitted to the municipal police.

gizlilik_h6: 6. Transfer of Data to Third Parties (Domestic and International)

gizlilik_p8: Your personal data is stored for the period required by the purpose of processing or the legal statute of limitations (usually 10 years) stipulated in the relevant legislation (Condominium Law, Turkish Commercial Code, Code of Obligations, etc.). kvkk_page_desc: The security and privacy of your personal data is a top priority for us.
kvkk_p1: Alo Management Services Inc. As such, in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 ("KVKK"), your personal data will be recorded, stored, updated, disclosed / transferred to third parties where the legislation allows, classified and processed in the ways listed in the KVKK, within the framework explained in this clarification text.
kvkk_p2: Your collected personal data is processed for the purposes of carrying out the necessary work by our business units to benefit you from the services offered by our company, tracking site management fees, carrying out legal processes and ensuring building security (CCTV records, license plate recognition).
kvkk_h3: 3. To whom and for what purpose the processed data can be transferred
kvkk_p3: Your personal data may be transferred to authorized public institutions and organizations in order to fulfill our legal obligations, to our company lawyers to resolve legal disputes, and to contracted banks for dues collection processes.
kvkk_p4: To exercise your rights under Article 11 of the KVKK, you can contact us at kvkk@aloyonetim.com.tr.
kvkk_p5:
Your personal data is collected based on the processing conditions specified in Articles 5 and 6 of the KVKK. These are basically:
- It is clearly foreseen in the laws (Condominium Law etc.),
- It is directly related to the establishment or execution of a contract (Execution of the management contract),
- It is mandatory for the data controller to fulfill its legal obligation,
- It is necessary to process data for the legitimate interests of the data controller, provided that it does not harm the fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject.
kvkk_h6: 6. Methods of Collection of Personal Data
kvkk_p6: Your data is collected in physical and digital environments. These are: Information update forms that you fill out and submit to the management office, notifications made via e-mail and call center, legal notifications from official institutions (Land Registry Offices, Population Directorates), registration/payment screens on our website/mobile application, PTS cameras at vehicle entrances and common area security cameras.
kvkk_h7: 7. Data Processing with Camera (CCTV) and Security Systems
kvkk_p7: In the sites that our company manages, 24/7 security camera monitoring is carried out in common areas (entrance doors, lobby, parking lot, elevator interiors, garden) in order to ensure building security and crime prevention. Warning signs "Monitored by Camera 24/7" are visibly hung in the camera recording areas. The cameras are positioned in such a way that they cannot see the inside of the apartment (private areas). Camera recordings are stored for an average of 15-30 days and are automatically deleted by the system.
kvkk_h8: 8. Use of License Plate Recognition System (PTS)
kvkk_p8: PTS is used to ensure security in the parking areas of your site and to speed up transitions. Your vehicle license plates are defined as 'Authorized Vehicle' in our system. This data is processed only for the purpose of ensuring site security and is not shared with any institution or organization unless there is a legal investigation (Police, Prosecutor's Office).
kvkk_h9: 9. Parties to which Personal Data May Be Transferred
kvkk_p9:
Your data; It can only be transferred to achieve the purposes described above and within the limits specified in Article 8 of the KVKK:
- To Law Offices and Lawyers with whom the Company has a contract for enforcement proceedings and resolution of legal disputes,
- To Financial Advisors and Independent Audit Firms for tax and financial audits,
- To domestic/foreign companies from which we receive server (hosting), SMS integrator and cloud computing services to provide digital services. to suppliers,
- In case of legal request, to Authorized Public Institutions and Organizations such as Police Departments, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, SSI, Tax Offices.
kvkk_p10: Since the cloud-based servers (AWS, Azure, etc.), e-mail servers (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365) and WhatsApp communication channels used in our systems are located abroad, your data can be transferred abroad by taking the necessary administrative and technical security measures in accordance with Article 9 of the KVKK, due to the necessity of using relevant technologies.
kvkk_h11: 11. Rights of the Relevant Person (Data Owner)
kvkk_p11:
In accordance with Article 11 of the KVKK, you have the following rights as the data owner:
a) Learning whether personal data is being processed,
b) Requesting information if the data has been processed,
c) Learning the purpose of processing and whether it is used in accordance with its purpose,
d) Knowing the third parties to whom it is transferred domestically or abroad,
e) Requesting correction of the data if it is incomplete or incorrectly processed,
f) KVKK. Requesting the deletion or destruction of the data within the framework of the conditions in Article 7,
g) Objecting to a result against you arising from the analysis of the processed data exclusively through automatic systems,
h) Requesting compensation for the damage if you suffer damage due to unlawful processing.
kvkk_h12: 12. Exercise of Rights and Application Method
kvkk_p12: In order to exercise your rights and submit your requests specified in Article 11 of the KVKK, you can send an e-mail to info@aloyonetim.com.tr via your e-mail address registered in our system. Our company will finalize the request free of charge as soon as possible and within thirty (30) days at the latest, depending on the nature of the request.

hfq_s1_q: What is the legal late-payment interest if complex or building dues are not paid?
hfq_s1_a: Under Article 20 of the Condominium Law, a statutory late-payment compensation of 5% per month applies to unpaid dues and advance payments. After the second notice, the Alo Yönetim legal department starts enforcement proceedings directly for overdue dues.
hfq_s2_q: Is it mandatory to obtain a green label in periodic elevator inspections?
hfq_s2_a: Yes. Under the Ministry of Industry and Technology Elevator Regulation, an inspection by a Type A accredited inspection body is carried out once a year. A green label indicates that life and property safety are fully ensured; elevators with a red label are sealed.
hfq_s3_q: Can a guard or watchman work in a complex without a private security ID?
hfq_s3_a: Under the Private Security Law No. 5188, providing uniformed and authorised security service requires a Governorate Private Security Permit (ÖGİ) and certified personnel. Otherwise the complex management may face heavy administrative fines.
hfq_s4_q: Under Article 37 of the Condominium Law, how many days is the objection period for the operating budget, and what is its enforcement effect?
hfq_s4_a: The objection period for the operating budget served to unit owners is a strict 7 days. A budget not objected to within 7 days becomes final, has the effect of an acknowledgment of debt within the meaning of Article 68 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law, and can be taken directly to enforcement without a court judgment.
hfq_s5_q: What is biocidal pest treatment, and is it mandatory in buildings and complexes?
hfq_s5_a: Biocidal pest treatment is the elimination of insects and rodents with formulations approved by the Turkish Ministry of Health, without harming human or environmental health. Under the Biocidal Products Regulation, in shared living areas it may only be carried out by companies licensed by the Ministry of Health.
